en.name: Tempeh, frozen
en.summary: Frozen tempeh keeps 6 months from purchase at −18 °C (0 °F) for best quality. Keep it frozen and cook as directed. Once cooked, it keeps 3–4 days in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below.
en.pantry: No room-temperature storage. Tempeh is a live fermented food — whole soybeans bound together by a mould culture — and at room temperature that culture carries on working, which is why a fresh block sporulates and turns black in a warm kitchen within a day. It is also moist, low-acid and high in protein, so anything left out is in the danger zone of 4–60 °C (40–140 °F) and follows the two-hour rule, one hour above 32 °C (90 °F). Keep it cold and cook it through.
en.fridge: 3–4 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below after cooking, covered. Unopened fresh tempeh follows its own printed date; once opened, wrap it tightly and use it within a few days, because the exposed surface dries and any loose beans go first. Black or grey patches on the surface of a fresh block are the culture sporulating and are normal — a sharp ammonia smell is not, and means the block has gone too far.
en.freezer: 6 months from purchase at −18 °C (0 °F) for best quality. Freezing stops the culture entirely, which is exactly why frozen tempeh holds its character better than refrigerated tempeh does. Kept continuously at −18 °C it stays safe indefinitely; the window describes drying and freezer burn. Slice or cube the block before freezing — a frozen block is very hard to cut — and bag the pieces flat with the air pressed out.
en.thawing: Thaw in the fridge, or cook straight from frozen if the pieces are already sliced. Never thaw on the counter. Tempeh thawed in the fridge and still at or below 4 °C (40 °F) may be refrozen with some quality loss; anything thawed warm must not be refrozen.
spoilage: A sharp ammonia smell, which is the clearest sign it has gone too far.
Pink, yellow, orange or blue growth on the surface, as opposed to the normal white or black-grey culture.
A slimy or wet surface on a thawed block.
Dry, pale, crumbling patches after long freezing — freezer burn.
tips: Slice or cube before freezing; a frozen block is almost impossible to cut.
Black and grey patches are the culture doing its job, not spoilage.
Steam or simmer briefly before frying if you want a softer texture.
Cook it through rather than eating it raw.

faq.q: How long does frozen tempeh last?
faq.a: 6 months from purchase at −18 °C (0 °F) for best quality. Kept continuously frozen it stays safe beyond that, but it dries and freezer-burns.

faq.q: Is black mould on tempeh a problem?
faq.a: No. Black or grey patches are the culture sporulating and are normal. A sharp ammonia smell, or pink, orange or blue growth, is the sign to throw it out.

faq.q: Can you cook tempeh from frozen?
faq.a: Yes, if it is already sliced or cubed. Otherwise thaw it in the fridge first, never on the counter.

zh.name: 冷凍天貝
zh.summary: 冷凍天貝在 −18 °C 下自購買日起可保有最佳品質 6 個月。請保持冷凍並依指示烹調。煮熟之後放 4 °C 以下冷藏 3～4 天。
zh.pantry: 沒有室溫保存這一項。天貝是活的發酵食品——整顆黃豆被黴菌菌絲黏成一塊——而在室溫下菌種會繼續工作，所以一塊新鮮天貝在溫暖的廚房裡一天內就會開始產孢、變黑。它同時也是含水量高、低酸、高蛋白的食物，任何擺在外面的都在 4～60 °C 的危險溫度帶裡，適用兩小時原則，超過 32 °C 只有一小時。請保持低溫並煮熟再吃。
zh.fridge: 煮熟之後蓋好放 4 °C 以下 3～4 天。未拆封的新鮮天貝依包裝上的日期；拆封後請包緊，並在幾天內用掉，因為露出來的切面會變乾，鬆落的豆子也最先壞。新鮮天貝表面出現黑色或灰色斑塊，是菌種在產孢，屬於正常——但刺鼻的氨味不是，那表示它已經走太遠了。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下自購買日起 6 個月品質最好。冷凍會讓菌種完全停下來，這也正是冷凍天貝比冷藏天貝更能維持原本風味的原因。全程維持在 −18 °C 就一直是安全的；這個期限描述的是變乾和凍燒。冷凍前先切片或切塊——整塊凍硬之後非常難切——然後平放裝袋、壓出空氣。
zh.thawing: 放冷藏解凍；如果已經切片，也可以從冷凍直接下鍋。絕對不要在檯面上解凍。在冷藏解凍、且維持在 4 °C 以下的可以再冷凍，只是品質打折；回溫過的絕對不行。
spoilage: 刺鼻的氨味，這是它走過頭最明確的訊號。
表面長出粉紅、黃色、橘色或藍色的菌落（正常的是白色或黑灰色菌絲）。
解凍後的天貝表面黏滑或濕答答。
冷凍太久出現乾燥、發白、碎裂的斑塊——那是凍燒。
tips: 冷凍前先切片或切塊；凍硬的整塊幾乎切不動。
黑色和灰色斑塊是菌種在工作，不是壞掉。
想要口感軟一點，下鍋煎之前先蒸或煮一下。

faq.a: −18 °C 下自購買日起 6 個月品質最好。只要沒退冰放更久仍然安全，但會變乾、凍燒。

faq.q: 天貝上的黑霉有問題嗎？
faq.a: 沒有。黑色或灰色斑塊是菌種產孢，屬於正常。刺鼻氨味，或粉紅、橘、藍色菌落，才是該丟的訊號。

faq.q: 天貝可以從冷凍直接煮嗎？
faq.a: 已經切片或切塊的可以。整塊的請先放冷藏解凍，絕對不要放檯面。
